ns2:course.label: Minoritarian Aesthetics Practicum
ns2:course.description: Following a minoritarian aesthetics compass, informed by the disciplines of relational ethnic and performance studies, students will approach critical theory, embodied practice, and collective learning as inseparable. Working closely with one another and with guest artists, scholars, teachers, and curators, as well as practice-based initiatives such as the Mellon funded Minor Aesthetics Lab, students will be asked to display and/or perform their work within the tradition of fusing aesthetics and social life. Same as AAS 495, ENGL 495, GWS 425, and THEA 468. 3 undergraduate hours. 4 graduate hours.
